title: Burst reshuffle latency investigation (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: quick notebook-style log for the burst-reshuffle tail-latency we keep seeing on Dedicated pools when autoscaler moves jobs between hosts. Not a formal report — notes to iterate and hand off to SRE/infra.

Background / hypothesis
- Repro: repeated customer traffic pattern (sudden +40% QPS for ~90s every 15m) triggers burst capacity which reshuffles pods across a warm pool. During reshuffle we see p95->p99 spikes (200ms->1.8s) for some requests.
- Hypothesis A: KV cache warmup penalty + mutex contention on host-level disk I/O during container startup.
- Hypothesis B: Network TCP warmup + TLS handshake when routing flips to new host (cold TLS context in some edge cases).
- Hypothesis C: Scheduler-induced co-location causing GPU oversubscription briefly; GPU kernel queues stall then flush.

Quick environment summary (experiment run 2026-03-09)
- model: small-gen-v1 (16k context, 8-bit quant)
- pool: dedicated-warmpool-4g (4xA100 logical), reserved 12 workers, autoscale policy: add 2 workers on burst, reshuffle policy: pack_then_spread
- client load: poisson arrivals mean 18 qps baseline, bursts to 25 qps over ~90s
- payload: mean tokens in/out 64 tokens; streaming disabled
- runtime config tweaks tested: batcher.max_batch_size=8, batcher.batch_timeout_ms=6, kvcache.enabled=true, prefetch=true

Experiment run log (raw timeline)
- 08:00 TTL check: baseline stable, p95 ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 240ms
- 08:14 incoming ramp starts (synthetic load generator)
- 08:15 autoscaler spins two additional workers; reshuffle initiated at 08:16:12
- 08:16:18 first client-side 504s observed (short spikes) -- concurrent with pod drain of worker-3
- 08:16:30 sustained tail at p99 ~ 1800ms for ~48s
- 08:18 autoscaler settles, workers up, p99 returns to ~260ms
- Observed correlation: p99 spike begins ~6s after reshuffle start and lasts ~50s

Measurements collected
- KV cache hit rate (per-host): host-A: 82%->15% during reshuffle; host-B: 45%->70% after warmup
- GPU util: slight dip on new hosts for 12s while workloads balance; no maxed-out GPU observed (peak 68%)
- Syscalls: increased open()/close() patterns during 08:16-08:17 (suggests file-backed KV cache miss path)
- TCP connections: new connections peaked +54% for 18s around reshuffle window
- TLS handshake latencies: median TLS handshake increased from 8ms->56ms during reshuffle for new connections

Small CSV-style snippets captured (excerpt):

08:17 | ===|

What I tried (fast experiments)
1) Force warm prefetch on new workers: kvcache.prefetch_on_attach=true
   - Result: reduced duration of p99 spike by ~20s in 2/3 runs. KV hit warmed faster but increased disk IO bursts.
2) Increase batcher.batch_timeout_ms from 6->12 in new workers until steady state
   - Result: slightly higher median latency (+15ms) but reduced p99 amplitude by ~260ms. Tradeoff acceptable for some SLAs.
3) Keep-alive connection pool bump (proxy-level): keepalive.max_idle=200 -> reduced number of new TLS handshakes per reshuffle by ~70%
   - Result: handshake spike removed for clients that reused connections; some clients still created new connections (curl-like) -> residual tail persisted.
4) Experiment: no-reshuffle run (disabled pack_then_spread) — simulate scale-up-only policy
   - Result: p99 spike eliminated in synthetic runs but increases steady-state cost by 12% (expected).

Preliminary conclusions
- Primary contributors: KV cache cold miss path + connection churn (TLS) when reshuffle routes requests to newly-attached hosts.
- GPU oversubscription appears unlikely (util never maxed), though short kernel-queue jitter cannot be fully ruled out.
- Short-term mitigations with low-risk: prefetch_on_attach + increase batch timeout + proxy keepalive tuning.
- Long-term: change reshuffle policy to a slower ramp (graceful attach window), or ensure pre-warmed ephemeral cache images on new hosts (snapshot kvcache state), or sticky routing for short-lived bursts.

Open questions
- Can we snapshot kvcache across warmpool instances cheaply? Disk/rsync latency and security concerns.
- Is there a way to decouple TLS warmups e.g., session ticket reuse across hosts? Need security review.
- For customer traffic shapes (many curl-like one-off connections), will keepalive-level fixes be sufficient?
- Do other models with larger KV cache size show worse penalties? need to run scaling matrix (1x/2x/4x cache)

Next runs to schedule (short list)
- A: Repeat the prefetch_on_attach test but with kvcache stored in tmpfs to eliminate disk open()/close() spikes — measure IO and p99. (CRITICAL: monitor memory pressure)
- B: Run reshuffle with keepalive enforced (client sim forced to reuse connections) to isolate TLS effect.
- C: Run with batch_timeout=20ms on 1/3 traffic to evaluate median tradeoff vs tail improvement.
- D: Run the same pattern on model medium-gen-v2 to check cache-size scaling.

Quick ops checklist to hand off to SRE
- Add temporary config flag to warmpool that enables kvcache.prefetch_on_attach for 72h on staging.
- Schedule a controlled reshuffle window at 03:00 UTC with synthetic bursts and GRPC probe enabled.
- Collect the ring-buffer traces for open()/close(), TLS handshake times, and per-request KV miss traces.

Notes to self (scratchy)
- Don't forget to tag JIRA-4821 with results and link graphs.
- Slack thread #serving-runtime: paste p99 CSV and short timeline snapshot.
- If prefetch helps but disk I/O becomes noisy, consider tmpfs prototype then cost estimate.

- scripts used: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-scripts/blob/main/reshuffle-run.sh

End of scratchpad. Will formalize into a one-pager if we converge on a recommended mitigation.
